1 Chapter 10 Random Regressors

1.1 10.1 The Instrumental Variables (IV) Method

library(PoEdata)
data(mroz)
mroz1 = mroz[mroz$wage>0,]
mhist(mroz1$wage)

mhist(mroz1$wage %>% log)

library(lmtest)
## Loading required package: zoo
## 
## Attaching package: 'zoo'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
## 
##     as.Date, as.Date.numeric
mroz1.ols = lm(log(wage)~educ+exper+I(exper^2), data = mroz1)
reset(mroz1.ols)
## 
##  RESET test
## 
## data:  mroz1.ols
## RESET = 1.6333, df1 = 2, df2 = 422, p-value = 0.1965
bptest(mroz1.ols)
## 
##  studentized Breusch-Pagan test
## 
## data:  mroz1.ols
## BP = 11.709, df = 3, p-value = 0.008449
shapiro.test(mroz1.ols$residuals)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  mroz1.ols$residuals
## W = 0.93329, p-value = 6.629e-13
mhist(mroz1.ols$residuals)

# educ parece ser endógena
# está com o coeficiente possivelmente enviesado
mroz1.ols %>% summary
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = log(wage) ~ educ + exper + I(exper^2), data = mroz1)
## 
## Residuals:
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -3.08404 -0.30627  0.04952  0.37498  2.37115 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) -0.5220406  0.1986321  -2.628  0.00890 ** 
## educ         0.1074896  0.0141465   7.598 1.94e-13 ***
## exper        0.0415665  0.0131752   3.155  0.00172 ** 
## I(exper^2)  -0.0008112  0.0003932  -2.063  0.03974 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.6664 on 424 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.1568, Adjusted R-squared:  0.1509 
## F-statistic: 26.29 on 3 and 424 DF,  p-value: 1.302e-15
# introduzir mothereduc na equação
library(AER)
## Loading required package: car
## Loading required package: carData
## Loading required package: sandwich
## Loading required package: survival
mroz1.iv <- ivreg(
  # regressão original
  log(wage)~educ+exper+I(exper^2) |
  # defino o(s) instrumento(s)
  exper+I(exper^2)+mothereduc,
  # usar mothereduc como instrumento para educ
  data=mroz1)
mroz1.iv %>% summary
## 
## Call:
## ivreg(formula = log(wage) ~ educ + exper + I(exper^2) | exper + 
##     I(exper^2) + mothereduc, data = mroz1)
## 
## Residuals:
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -3.10804 -0.32633  0.06024  0.36772  2.34351 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)   
## (Intercept)  0.1981861  0.4728772   0.419  0.67535   
## educ         0.0492630  0.0374360   1.316  0.18891   
## exper        0.0448558  0.0135768   3.304  0.00103 **
## I(exper^2)  -0.0009221  0.0004064  -2.269  0.02377 * 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.6796 on 424 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-Squared: 0.1231,  Adjusted R-squared: 0.1169 
## Wald test: 7.348 on 3 and 424 DF,  p-value: 8.228e-05
eq1 = educ~exper+I(exper^2)+mothereduc+fathereduc
lm(eq1, data = mroz1) -> meq1
educhat = predict(meq1)
lm(log(wage)~educhat+exper+I(exper^2), data = mroz1) -> wage.2sls;  wage.2sls %>% summary
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = log(wage) ~ educhat + exper + I(exper^2), data = mroz1)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -3.1631 -0.3539  0.0326  0.3818  2.3727 
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)   
## (Intercept)  0.0481003  0.4197565   0.115  0.90882   
## educhat      0.0613966  0.0329624   1.863  0.06321 . 
## exper        0.0441704  0.0140844   3.136  0.00183 **
## I(exper^2)  -0.0008990  0.0004212  -2.134  0.03338 * 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.7075 on 424 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.04978,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.04306 
## F-statistic: 7.405 on 3 and 424 DF,  p-value: 7.615e-05
mroz1.iv1 <- ivreg(
  # regressão original
  log(wage)~educ+exper+I(exper^2) |
  # defino o(s) instrumento(s)
  exper+I(exper^2)+mothereduc+fathereduc,
  # usar mothereduc + fathereduc como instrumento para educ
  data=mroz1)
mroz1.iv1 %>% summary
## 
## Call:
## ivreg(formula = log(wage) ~ educ + exper + I(exper^2) | exper + 
##     I(exper^2) + mothereduc + fathereduc, data = mroz1)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -3.0986 -0.3196  0.0551  0.3689  2.3493 
## 
## Coefficients:

## (Intercept)  0.0481003  0.4003281   0.120  0.90442   
## educ         0.0613966  0.0314367   1.953  0.05147 . 
## exper        0.0441704  0.0134325   3.288  0.00109 **
## I(exper^2)  -0.0008990  0.0004017  -2.238  0.02574 * 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.6747 on 424 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-Squared: 0.1357,  Adjusted R-squared: 0.1296 
## Wald test: 8.141 on 3 and 424 DF,  p-value: 2.787e-05
mroz1.iv2 <- ivreg(
  # regressão original
  log(wage)~educ+exper+I(exper^2) |
  # defino o(s) instrumento(s)
  exper+I(exper^2)+fathereduc,
  # usar fathereduc como instrumento para educ
  data=mroz1)
mroz1.iv2 %>% summary
## 
## Call:

stargazer(mroz1.ols, wage.2sls, mroz1.iv, mroz1.iv1,

2 Chapter 11 Simultaneous Equations Models

he following example uses the dataset truffles, where
q is quantity of truffles traded,
p is the market price,
ps is the price of a substitute,
di is disposable income, and
pf is a measure of costs of production. The structural demand and supply equations (Equations 1 and 2) are formulated based on economic theory; quantity and price are endogenous, and all the other variables are considered exogenous.

\[ \text{Equação da demanda: }\quad q = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1p + \alpha_2ps+\alpha_3di+\epsilon_d\\ \alpha_1 (-)\quad\alpha_2 (+)\quad\alpha_3 (+)\quad\\ \text{Equação da oferta: }\quad q = \beta_0 + \beta_1p + \beta_2pf + \epsilon_s\\ \beta_1 (+)\quad\beta_2 (-) \]

data("truffles", package="PoEdata")
truffles %>% head
##       p     q    ps    di    pf
## 1 29.64 19.89 19.97 2.103 10.52
## 2 40.23 13.04 18.04 2.043 19.67
## 3 34.71 19.61 22.36 1.870 13.74
## 4 41.43 17.13 20.87 1.525 17.95
## 5 53.37 22.55 19.79 2.709 13.71
## 6 38.52  6.37 15.98 2.489 24.95
lm(q~p+ps+di, truffles) %>% summary
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = q ~ p + ps + di, data = truffles)
## 
## Residuals:
##    Min     1Q Median     3Q    Max 
## -7.155 -1.936 -0.374  2.396  6.335 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)   
## (Intercept)  1.09105    3.71158   0.294  0.77112   
## p            0.02330    0.07684   0.303  0.76418   
## ps           0.71004    0.21432   3.313  0.00272 **
## di           0.07644    1.19086   0.064  0.94931   
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 3.46 on 26 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.4957, Adjusted R-squared:  0.4375 
## F-statistic:  8.52 on 3 and 26 DF,  p-value: 0.0004159
lm(q~p+pf, truffles) %>% summary
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = q ~ p + pf, data = truffles)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -3.7830 -0.8530  0.2270  0.7579  3.3475 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) 20.03278    1.22197   16.39 1.47e-15 ***
## p            0.33799    0.02174   15.54 5.42e-15 ***
## pf          -1.00092    0.07639  -13.10 3.23e-13 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 1.498 on 27 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.9019, Adjusted R-squared:  0.8946 
## F-statistic: 124.1 on 2 and 27 DF,  p-value: 2.448e-14
D <- q~p+ps+di # ~ps+di+pf -> p é instrumentalizado por pf
S <- q~p+pf    # ~ps+di+pf -> p é instrumentalizado por ps+di
sys <- list(D,S)
library(systemfit)
## Loading required package: Matrix
## 
## Please cite the 'systemfit' package as:
## Arne Henningsen and Jeff D. Hamann (2007). systemfit: A Package for Estimating Systems of Simultaneous Equations in R. Journal of Statistical Software 23(4), 1-40. http://www.jstatsoft.org/v23/i04/.
## 
## If you have questions, suggestions, or comments regarding the 'systemfit' package, please use a forum or 'tracker' at systemfit's R-Forge site:
## https://r-forge.r-project.org/projects/systemfit/
systemfit(sys, data = truffles) %>% summary
## 
## systemfit results 
## method: OLS 
## 
##         N DF     SSR detRCov   OLS-R2 McElroy-R2
## system 60 53 371.764 23.5756 0.698799   0.808917
## 
##      N DF      SSR      MSE    RMSE       R2   Adj R2
## eq1 30 26 311.2096 11.96960 3.45971 0.495720 0.437534
## eq2 30 27  60.5546  2.24276 1.49758 0.901878 0.894610
## 
## The covariance matrix of the residuals
##          eq1     eq2
## eq1 11.96960 1.80814
## eq2  1.80814 2.24276
## 
## The correlations of the residuals
##         eq1     eq2
## eq1 1.00000 0.34898
## eq2 0.34898 1.00000
## 
## 
## OLS estimates for 'eq1' (equation 1)
## Model Formula: q ~ p + ps + di
## 
##              Estimate Std. Error t value  Pr(>|t|)   
## (Intercept) 1.0910453  3.7115804 0.29396 0.7711247   
## p           0.0232954  0.0768423 0.30316 0.7641812   
## ps          0.7100395  0.2143246 3.31292 0.0027193 **
## di          0.0764442  1.1908551 0.06419 0.9493078   
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 3.459711 on 26 degrees of freedom
## Number of observations: 30 Degrees of Freedom: 26 
## SSR: 311.209627 MSE: 11.969601 Root MSE: 3.459711 
## Multiple R-Squared: 0.49572 Adjusted R-Squared: 0.437534 
## 
## 
## OLS estimates for 'eq2' (equation 2)
## Model Formula: q ~ p + pf
## 
##               Estimate Std. Error  t value   Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) 20.0327764  1.2219720  16.3938 1.3323e-15 ***
## p            0.3379875  0.0217445  15.5435 5.3291e-15 ***
## pf          -1.0009246  0.0763902 -13.1028 3.2352e-13 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 1.497585 on 27 degrees of freedom
## Number of observations: 30 Degrees of Freedom: 27 
## SSR: 60.554565 MSE: 2.242762 Root MSE: 1.497585 
## Multiple R-Squared: 0.901878 Adjusted R-Squared: 0.89461
# defino os instrumentos
instr <- ~ps+di+pf
# vou analisar a relação q~p
truff.sys <- systemfit(sys, inst=instr, method="2SLS", data=truffles)

2.1 Fulton Fish

\[ \log(quan) = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1\log(price)+\alpha_2mon+\alpha_3tue+\alpha_4wed+\alpha_5thu+\epsilon_d\\ \log(quan) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\log(price)+\beta_2stormy+\epsilon_s\\ \log(quan) = \gamma_0+\alpha_2mon+\alpha_3tue+\alpha_4wed+\alpha_5thu+\beta_2stormy+\epsilon_{r1}\\ \log(price) = \gamma_0+\alpha_2mon+\alpha_3tue+\alpha_4wed+\alpha_5thu+\beta_2stormy+\epsilon_{r1}\\ \]

2.2 LAVAAN

# resolve equações estruturais pelo método de covariância (CB-SEM)
library(lavaan)
## Warning: package 'lavaan' was built under R version 4.3.3
## This is lavaan 0.6-19
## lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
model = "
lprice~mon+dsi1*tue+dsi2*wed+thu+stormy
lquan~prec*lprice+mon+tue+wed+thu+stormy
tuemediado := dsi1*prec
wedmediado := dsi2*prec
"
sem(model = model, data = fultonfish) -> fit
summary(fit, standar = TRUE)
